projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sharp increase from 18 to 24 connected devices between 16:28 and 16:32, combined with zero camera activity, indicates a group of guests or family members arrived and entered through a non-camera-covered entry like a garage. This explains the sustained high device count and aligns with typical Sunday afternoon gatherings.

The sustained presence of 17-22 devices paired with zero camera activity suggests the household is likely gathered in a camera-blind zone or the presence sensors are counting smart home hubs rather than actual people; verifying camera status and checking a blind spot is recommended.

The sustained presence count of 22–26 devices paired with zero camera activity on a Sunday morning strongly indicates the presence sensor is likely detecting external Wi-Fi/Bluetooth probes or standby IoT devices rather than actual occupancy, as a family of four with two active dogs would typically trigger at least one camera. Cross-referencing presence with motion/light sensors is recommended to prevent false occupancy assumptions.

The sustained presence count of ~24–26 devices combined with zero camera activity on a Sunday morning suggests the presence metric is likely counting IoT/smart home devices rather than actual people, or the household is clustered in a camera-blind zone. This mismatch may cause automation logic to misinterpret occupancy and warrants a quick sensor calibration check.

The connected device count has dropped to 19 and is fluctuating, paired with zero camera activity on a Sunday morning. This pattern suggests the family may have left early or the Wi-Fi presence tracking is experiencing significant dropout, warranting a quick check to confirm the home's occupancy status.

The steady decline in connected devices (25 to 22) over the last 2.5 hours, paired with zero camera activity, confirms the household is still in a quiet wake-up phase with no one leaving yet. The consistently high device count likely reflects weekend guests or IoT devices, but no action is required.

The recent ~9-hour sleep reports for both adults, combined with zero motion/camera and sustained device presence, confirms the household is in a prolonged sleep state; the high device count is expected (phones on nightstands) and explains the earlier presence correlation flag.

The sustained presence of 24–26 mobile devices with zero motion or camera activity at this late hour strongly indicates a completed gathering where guests have physically departed but left their phones connected to the home Wi-Fi. This resolves the high device count anomaly as a normal post-event state, though monitoring for a drop by morning is prudent.

The sustained presence of 24–26 mobile devices combined with zero camera or motion activity late on a Saturday strongly indicates a house gathering or sleepover, with guests and family settled in rooms outside camera view. This explains the high device count and lack of activity, confirming expected weekend occupancy beyond the core household.

High device connectivity (24–26) paired with zero motion or camera activity for four hours suggests the household is likely gathered in a single, non-monitored space (e.g., home theater or basement) or has disabled motion tracking, but the complete lack of physical activity warrants a quick wellness check to rule out sensor blind spots or unresponsiveness.
